First real-hardware test of the Web Serial transport prototype (webRAW-Serial.cpp) - near-solid-color content (flat fill + a thin moving stripe), ~362:1 compression ratio, not representative of real screen content. Zero crashes, zero drops across 60 frames. prep_avg_ms (Swap) derived by subtraction (total_avg_ms - recv_avg_ms - decode_decompress_avg_ms - push_avg_ms) since this run's parser did not separately capture Swap= - not directly regex-extracted like the other columns. gaps_over_500ms_count/max_gap_ms not computed for this run. See webRAW-Serial_amoled_t4_gradient row for the same board/protocol under much less compressible, more realistic content.

Animated diagonal RGB gradient (smooth per-pixel color, phase-shifted each frame) - ~16:1 compression ratio (33.4KB avg compressed from 540KB raw), much more representative of real video/photo content than the flatfill row. Found and fixed a real firmware bug getting here: the first attempt at this exact test corrupted every frame after the first (RX buffer overflow - see webRAW-Serial.cpp setRxBufferSize comment) because loop() blocks ~80ms inside drawRawFrame() every frame, during which a 33KB USB burst (native USB CDC ignores the nominal 115200 baud - it transmitted in ~61ms) could overflow the previous 16KB RX queue entirely. Fixed by sizing the queue to 65536 bytes. Zero drops/decode-failures/resyncs/crashes across 80 frames after the fix. One transient host-side USB disconnect (not a device crash - confirmed alive via a liveness probe showing continuous uptime) hit an earlier, unpaced attempt at this same test; this row is the successful retry with a small 30ms pacing gap between sends. gaps_over_500ms_count/max_gap_ms measure test-script send-to-send gaps (immediately after each ack), not a separately-logged device metric - a reasonable proxy here since sends are back-to-back, but not the same measurement method as the WS-based rows' device-observed inter-frame gaps. Timing stats (recv/decompress/swap/push/total) captured from n=61 of the 80 acked frames' log lines - the log-scanning parser does not guarantee capturing every single line; all 80 sends were still confirmed acked by the protocol itself, independent of how many log lines were captured for timing.

Same animated gradient content/generator as webRAW-Serial_amoled_t4_gradient (this repo's Web Serial transport prototype) and the same T4-S3 board, driven over WebSocket via a Python client (websockets lib) instead of a real browser - a direct apples-to-apples transport comparison. Real finding: despite the client waiting for each ack before sending the next frame (proper wait-mode client behavior), the drop rate (63.29%) is close to webRAW_amoled_immediate's territory (69.75%), not webRAW_amoled_wait's (14.96%). Root cause: client->text("a") fires as soon as the WS message is reassembled, well before loop() finishes rendering it (Total~160ms here) - the ack means "I received your bytes", not "I finished the previous frame", so wait-mode pacing does not actually gate on render completion. The original wait-mode row's low drop rate likely depended on that row's much faster compute_total_avg_ms (56.17ms there vs 118.9ms here) leaving less room for this race to matter, not on wait-mode being inherently more effective for this content. gaps_over_500ms_count/max_gap_ms computed from combined render+drop event timestamps in the serial log, not just render events.

Same 80-frame animated diagonal-gradient content as webRAW_amoled_t4_gradient and webRAW-Serial_amoled_t4_gradient, encoded to H.264 via ffmpeg/libx264 (Constrained Baseline, level 3.0, annexb, 700kbps, 5fps, keyframe every 10 frames = 2s, matching stream.html defaults exactly) rather than captured from a real browser VideoEncoder - a Python client parsed the Annex-B stream into per-frame access-unit chunks (SPS+PPS+IDR bundled for the 8 keyframes, single slice NAL for the 72 delta frames) and sent one chunk per WS message to /video-stream with maxInFlight=1 ack-wait pacing, matching stream.html's default. All 80/80 frames rendered with zero drops and zero "No frame" lines - unlike webRAW_amoled_t4_gradient's WS-based ack-on-receipt issue, this protocol's ack fires only after decode+push complete (tAcked measured from tPushed), so ack-wait pacing here is genuinely drop-proof by construction, not just by luck. The tradeoff is speed: software H.264 decode dominates compute (avg 318.6ms/frame, vs raw deflate's 37.3ms on the same content/hardware) for a 6.6x lower achieved_fps (2.51 vs raw's 6.23) despite H.264's much smaller payload (avg 15.5KB/frame vs raw's ~33KB) - this pipeline is bandwidth-efficient but CPU-decode-bound on this hardware, the opposite bottleneck from webRAW. gaps_over_500ms_count=7/max_gap_ms=711 track the periodic keyframes (52KB IDR decode is slower than a 10-15KB P-frame).

Same 80-frame animated diagonal-gradient content and Python-WS-client methodology as the webRAW_amoled_t4_gradient/webH264_amoled_t4_gradient rows (zlib deflate matching CompressionStream('deflate-raw'), or PIL JPEG at quality=70 matching stream.html's canvas.toBlob default) - not a real browser capture. Figures are aggregated across 10 repeated back-to-back runs (not one capture) specifically to confirm run-to-run stability before trusting the numbers - frames_rendered/frames_dropped/frames_total are summed across all 10 runs (10x80=800 sent total), total_min_ms/total_max_ms are the true min/max across every individual rendered frame in that combined set, and sample_duration_s/achieved_fps are the average of the 10 runs' own per-session values (a single-frame-in-flight wait-mode fps isn't meaningful to sum across disjoint sessions the way a frame count is). Confirms the exact same ack-on-receipt bug found and fixed on webRAW.cpp (AMOLED) also existed here, unfixed - 72.3% drop rate, stable within 70.9-73.4% across all 10 runs (see webRAW-CYD_gradient_after_ackfix for the fixed comparison). decode_decompress_avg_ms/prep_avg_ms/push_avg_ms blank - same reason as the other webRAW-CYD rows: this firmware logs one combined "Decompress+Push" stage, held in compute_total_avg_ms instead.

Ack moved from immediately-on-receipt (WS_EVT_DATA) to after drawRawStrips() actually completes in loop(), plus a frameInFlight guard on the existing ACK_NUDGE watchdog so it can't fire mid-stream and reintroduce the same bug conditionally - identical fix pattern to webRAW.cpp. Result: 800/800 rendered, 0 drops, across all 10 runs. compute_total_avg_ms itself also dropped (45.19 to 40.76ms) as a side effect - no more CPU spent decoding/reassembling frames that were only ever going to be dropped.

Original design: every decoded JPEG MCU block (16x16px) is pushed straight to the display individually - ~300 separate tft.pushImage() calls per frame, no PSRAM for an intermediate buffer. push_avg_ms holds this firmware's "Render" field (the MCU-push loop itself, not a separate stage - see webJPEG-CYD.cpp), prep_avg_ms holds "Setup" (per-frame offset calc). Same ack-on-receipt bug as webRAW-CYD - 89.5% drop rate, stable within 88.6-89.9% across all 10 runs.

Figures are aggregated across 10 repeated back-to-back runs (not one capture) specifically to confirm run-to-run stability before trusting the numbers - frames_rendered/frames_dropped/frames_total are summed across all 10 runs (10x80=800 sent total), total_min_ms/total_max_ms are the true min/max across every individual rendered frame in that combined set, and sample_duration_s/achieved_fps are the average of the 10 runs' own per-session values (a single-frame-in-flight wait-mode fps isn't meaningful to sum across disjoint sessions the way a frame count is). Intermediate step: MCUs still decode straight to the display, but now batched into one push per MCU row (up to 320x16px, ~10KB buffer) instead of one push per individual 16x16 block - cuts ~300 pushes/frame to ~15. Render time drops (185.2ms to 162.5ms) from fewer, larger SPI transactions, and this was aimed at reducing the visible block-by-block "painting in" tearing effect (not independently confirmed - no camera on the physical display). Drop rate is still ~90% here, materially unchanged from before this row - the ack-on-receipt bug is a separate problem this specific change doesn't touch, see the next row.

Row-buffer optimization (previous row) plus the same ack-after-render fix as webRAW-CYD - this firmware has no ACK_NUDGE watchdog, so no frameInFlight gate was needed for that. Result: 800/800 rendered, 0 drops, across all 10 runs. Render time dropped further too (162.5 to 146.4ms), same CPU-contention-relief effect as webRAW-CYD's fix - no more wasted decode work on doomed frames. Together with the row-buffer change, this is a 3x lower Render time than the original per-MCU-block design (185.2 to 146.4ms) plus fully eliminated drops.
